'''Pierre Adrien Joliot-Curie''' ({{IPA|fr|pjɛʁ adʁjɛ̃ ʒɔljo kyʁi|lang}}; 12 March 1932 – 10 October 2026) was a French biologist and researcher for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]], specialising in photosynthesis.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pierre Joliot - Biographie et publications |url=https://www.college-de-france.fr/fr/chaire/pierre-joliot-bioenergetique-cellulaire-chaire-statutaire/biography |access-date= |website=Collège de France |at=under "Télecharger sa bibliographie"}}</ref> A researcher there since 1956, he became a Director of Research in 1974 and a member of their scientific council in 1992.<ref name="bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.evene.fr/celebre/biographie/pierre-joliot-13630.php|title=Biography @ Evene|date=12 March 1932 |accessdate=2007-01-24|language=fr}} [https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=fr&u=http://www.evene.fr/celebre/biographie/pierre-joliot-13630.php&sa=X&oi=translate&resnum=2&ct=result&prev=/search%3Fq%3DPierre%2BJoliot%26hl%3Den%26lr%3D%26sa%3DX Google translation]</ref> He was a scientific advisor to the French Prime Minister from 1985 to 1986 and was a member of [[Academia Europæa]]. He was made a commander of the [[Ordre National du Mérite]] (''English: the National Order of Merit'') in 1982 and of the [[Légion d'honneur]] (''English: Legion of Honor'') in 1984.<ref name="careertimeline">{{Cite web|url=http://www.college-de-france.fr/default/EN/all/ins_pro/p1029331983841.htm|title=Career Timeline|accessdate=2007-01-24|publisher=College of France|language=fr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080512144253/http://www.college-de-france.fr/default/EN/all/ins_pro/p1029331983841.htm |archive-date=2008-05-12|url-status=dead}} [https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=fr&u=https://web.archive.org/web/20080512144253/http://www.college-de-france.fr/default/EN/all/ins_pro/p1029331983841.htm&sa=X&oi=translate&resnum=3&ct=result&prev=/search%3Fq%3DPierre%2BJoliot%26hl%3Den%26lr%3D%26sa%3DX Google translation]</ref>

==Life and career==
Joliot came from the [[Curie family]] science dynasty. His grandparents, [[Marie Curie|Marie Sklodowska-Curie]] and [[Pierre Curie]] together with [[Henri Becquerel]] won the [[Nobel Prize]] in [[Physics]] in 1903 for their study of radioactivity. [[Marie Curie|Marie]] also won the Nobel Prize in [[Chemistry]] in 1911. Joliot's parents, [[Irène Joliot-Curie]] and [[Frédéric Joliot-Curie]], won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1935 for their discovery of [[induced radioactivity]]. His sister, [[Hélène Langevin-Joliot]], is a noted nuclear physicist.<ref name="familytree">{{Cite web|url=http://genealogy.links.org/links-cgi/readged?/home/ben/camilla-genealogy/current+c-joliot368+2-2-0-1-0|title=Family Tree|accessdate=2011-01-01|publisher=links.org}}</ref>

He held the Chair of Cellular Bioenergetics (1981–2002) at the [[Collège de France]] and was emeritus professor. He was also a member of the [[Academy of Science of France]]. In 2002, he published a work about his views on the research system, 'La Recherche Passionnément' (''English: Research Passionately'').

Joliot was married to biologist Anne (née Gricouroff) Joliot-Curie and they had two sons.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=m8S4bXj3dcMC&dq=alain+marc+joliot&pg=PA647 | New Scientist, 17 June 1976]{{deadlink|date=October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://gw.geneanet.org/wikifrat?lang=en&n=joliot&oc=0&p=pierre |title = Family tree of Pierre Joliot}}</ref> He died on 10 October 2026, at the age of 94.<ref>{{cite news |title=Le biologiste Pierre Joliot, découvreur de mécanismes fondamentaux de la photosynthèse et petit-fils de Pierre et Marie Curie, est mort |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/disparitions/article/2026/10/13/le-biologiste-pierre-joliot-decouvreur-des-mecanismes-fondamentaux-de-la-photosynthese-et-petit-fils-de-pierre-et-marie-curie-est-mort_6793144_3382.html |access-date=13 October 2026 |publisher=Le Monde |date=13 October 2026}}</ref>
